_header: File        : dispositions.json
Application : CardDemo
Type        : CI SUPPLY-CHAIN EVIDENCE
Function    : Per-advisory dispositions for the Maven BUILD PLUGIN graph,
consumed by scan_plugin_graph.py. Every HIGH or CRITICAL
finding either appears here with evidence and an expiry, or
it fails the build.
Derived from : pom.xml gap entry (2), which prescribes enumerating the
plugin graph and scanning it outside the build; and the
four-tier evidence discipline already established by
owasp-suppressions.xml for the APPLICATION graph.

_whatThisFileIsNot: It is NOT a suppression list. A suppression hides a finding; each entry here
states why the flagged code cannot execute in THIS build, names the evidence
that establishes it, and carries an expiry date after which the claim must be
re-argued or the dependency raised. An entry that matches nothing FAILS the
gate, so the file shrinks as the graph moves rather than accumulating.
It is also NOT the lever to reach for when the scan turns red. The scanner
reports the alternatives in its own failure message, in order of preference:
raise the plugin, or add an exact plugin-scoped dependency override of the
kind pom.xml already applies to the scanner's own HTTP transport. Adding an
entry here is the last option, not the first.

evidence: org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:12.1.0 because that goal reads the
plugin's own descriptor and is blind to project-level plugin
<dependencies> overrides. The plugin's REAL class realm, read from a
Maven -X run, loads httpclient5:jar:5.5.2 and httpcore5:jar:5.3.6, and
5.4.2 appears nowhere in it. This entry exists so that the scan measures
what executes; the scanner verifies the claim against the realm listing
and FAILS if the override is ever removed from pom.xml.

dispositions.tier: 1 - the flagged artifact is not the code that executes
dispositions.evidence: maven-core 3.6.3 is a compile-scope API dependency of dependency-check-maven 12.1.0; it is absent from that plugin's class realm. Measured from a Maven -X run: the realm lists 92 Included artifacts and maven-core, maven-plugin-api and maven-model are not among them, because Maven supplies its own core from the core realm to every plugin. The Maven that actually resolves dependencies here is 3.9.11, and the advisory is fixed in 3.8.1, so the behaviour that executes is already the fixed behaviour. Raising this is not possible without moving the AAP-pinned plugin root.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable feature is not exercised on untrusted input
dispositions.evidence: The defect is PropertyUtilsBean allowing the declared-class property of an enum to reach the classloader, so exploitation requires attacker-controlled bean property NAMES. This artefact reaches the graph only through maven-javadoc-plugin 3.11.2, maven-site-plugin 3.22.0 and dependency-check-maven 12.1.0, all of which introspect this project's own Maven model and its own report data at build time. No build-time input path carries a third-party-chosen property name. Fixed in 1.11.0, which none of the three plugin roots yet resolves; all three roots are AAP-pinned.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable feature is not enabled
dispositions.evidence: Both this advisory and GHSA-rmj7-2vxq-3g9f require POLYMORPHIC TYPING TO BE ENABLED, which owasp-suppressions.xml already establishes as the governing premise for the same two advisories on the application graph. Here the artefact arrives through dependency-check-maven 12.1.0, which deserializes the NVD advisory feed and its own report models with default typing; no polymorphic type validator is configured and no type identifier is honoured from the feed. Fixed in 2.20.1, which the AAP-pinned plugin root does not resolve.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable feature is not enabled
dispositions.evidence: BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.Builder.allowIfSubTypeIsArray() allowlists an array type without validating its component type, so the defect is unreachable unless polymorphic typing is enabled and that builder is used. dependency-check-maven 12.1.0 configures neither. Same premise and same tier as the application-graph entry in owasp-suppressions.xml.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable feature is not enabled
dispositions.evidence: The same advisory on the version spring-boot-maven-plugin 3.5.11 resolves. The plugin reads its own build metadata and this project's configuration when repackaging; polymorphic typing is not enabled on any of it. 2.19.4 is the version AAP section 0.6.1.2 records for jackson-bom, so the application graph carries the identical premise, already adjudicated in owasp-suppressions.xml.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable feature is not enabled
dispositions.evidence: As for CVE-2026-54512 on this coordinate: the array-component validation gap is reachable only through an enabled polymorphic type validator, and spring-boot-maven-plugin 3.5.11 configures none.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable class is not used
dispositions.evidence: The defect is uncontrolled CPU consumption in org.apache.commons.io.input.XmlStreamReader on maliciously crafted input. This artefact arrives through maven-compiler-plugin 3.14.1, maven-resources-plugin 3.3.1 and jacoco-maven-plugin 0.8.12, which use commons-io for ordinary file and stream copying over this project's own sources, resources and class files. XmlStreamReader exists to sniff the encoding of an untrusted XML stream, and no build-time path feeds it one. Fixed in 2.14.0; all three plugin roots are AAP-pinned and none yet resolves it.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable feature is not exercised on untrusted input
dispositions.evidence: Algorithmic denial of service when evaluating USER-SUPPLIED SpEL expressions. In the plugin graph this arrives through spring-boot-maven-plugin 3.5.11, which evaluates only expressions written in this repository's own pom.xml and configuration; a build has no untrusted expression author. Fixed in 6.2.19. NOTE, AND DISCLOSED SEPARATELY: the same coordinate and version are on the APPLICATION graph, where AAP section 0.6.1.2 pins spring 6.2.16, so the application-side exposure is a pinned-version residual risk recorded in DECISION_LOG.md and docs/validation-gates.md rather than a plugin-graph acceptance.

HTTP request smuggling through quoted-string parsing of chunked transfer-encoding extension values. Exploitation requires a running Jetty listener in front of a second HTTP hop. Jetty reaches this graph only through maven-site-plugin 3.22.0, whose embedded server starts only for the site:run preview goal, and no site goal is invoked anywhere in .github/workflows/build.yml or the Dockerfile - the documentation site is built by MkDocs, not by the Maven site plugin. So no listener exists to smuggle into. The fixes are 12.0.33 and 12.1.7: the 9.4 line has no fix, which is why the remedy is not to run the component rather than to raise it.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable parser mode is never constructed
dispositions.evidence: A maxNumberLength constraint bypass in the ASYNC (non-blocking) parser, reachable only through JsonFactory.createNonBlockingByteArrayParser fed attacker-chunked input. This version arrives through org.owasp:dependency-check-maven 12.1.0. Verified: the string createNonBlocking appears nowhere in this repository, and neither plugin constructs a non-blocking parser - the scanner deserializes the NVD feed and the repackager reads its own build metadata, both with the blocking parser. Fixed in 2.18.8 and 2.21.4; the plugin root that resolves this version is AAP-pinned and does not reach either.

Verified: the string createNonBlocking appears nowhere in this repository, and neither plugin constructs a non-blocking parser - the scanner deserializes the NVD feed and the repackager reads its own build metadata, both with the blocking parser. dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable code path is not fed untrusted input
dispositions.evidence: The Java Snappy and LZ4 decompressors can return previous output-buffer contents when handed malformed compressed input and the buffer is reused without clearing, so exploitation requires decompressing attacker-crafted Snappy or LZ4 data. This artefact arrives through maven-javadoc-plugin 3.11.2, which reads this project's own sources to generate API documentation and decompresses nothing supplied by a third party. Fixed in 2.0.3 and 3.4; the plugin root is AAP-pinned and resolves neither.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable format is never processed
dispositions.evidence: An unbounded OpenPGP AEAD chunk size permitting pre-authentication resource exhaustion, so exploitation requires parsing an attacker-supplied OpenPGP message. The bcpg module arrives through dependency-check-maven 12.1.0. Verified: this build signs and verifies nothing with OpenPGP - maven-gpg-plugin appears zero times in pom.xml - so no build step hands an OpenPGP message to this library. Fixed in 1.84, which the AAP-pinned plugin root does not resolve.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable cipher is never selected
dispositions.evidence: G3413CTRBlockCipher increments only the final counter byte, so the GOST 28147-2015 CTR keystream repeats after 255 blocks. Reachability requires selecting that specific Russian national cipher. Verified: neither GOST nor G3413 appears anywhere in this repository, and nothing in this build's cryptography selects it - the application's only cryptographic choices are BCrypt for password storage and the JWT signing algorithm. The artefact arrives through dependency-check-maven 12.1.0. Fixed in 1.80.2, 1.81.1 and 1.84, none resolved by the AAP-pinned plugin root.

dispositions.tier: 3 - the vulnerable method is not called on untrusted input
dispositions.evidence: Directory traversal in org.codehaus.plexus.util.Expand.extractFile, so exploitation requires expanding an attacker-supplied archive. This version arrives through org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin 0.8.12, all of which use plexus-utils for file scanning, XML reading and string handling over this project's own tree rather than for archive expansion. The only archive this build expands is the Maven distribution itself, and .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties pins it to an immutable Maven Central coordinate with a distributionSha256Sum verified before Maven runs, so its contents are not attacker-chosen. Fixed in 3.6.1 and 4.0.3; every plugin root carrying it is AAP-pinned.

DigestAuthentication.apply() in Jetty's HTTP CLIENT hashes credentials through ISO-8859-1, which silently substitutes any character above U+00FF and so permits an authentication bypass by character substitution. Reachability requires Jetty's HTTP client performing Digest authentication. Jetty reaches this graph only through maven-site-plugin 3.22.0, and no site goal is invoked anywhere in .github/workflows/build.yml or the Dockerfile - the documentation site is built by MkDocs. No Jetty client is ever constructed and no Digest exchange occurs. Unlike CVE-2026-2332 on jetty-http, this one IS fixed on the 9.4 line, at 9.4.63, but the version is chosen by the AAP-pinned site plugin rather than declared here.
